method: direct full-res crop inspection of the real rendered .pknob .cap element (knobzero-proof/<sid>-live-init.png) and the raw-sprite overlay (knobzero-proof/<sid>-raw-annotated.png), by eye, per verify-outputs-rule and this task's own framing ('the user's eye is the calibration'). Not a re-derivation of the detector's geometry -- a plain look at the pixels.

steam-porthole.note: triangle notch now visually symmetric and bisected by the stored angle -- tip points straight down at the disc center, base square to 12 o'clock. Direct fix confirmation for the exact skin the user flagged.

ps1-crunchy.note: small tick mark sits at 12 o'clock, at most 1-2deg off by eye. Both automated signals return NO-SIGNAL on this skin -- the theme's deliberately dithered/warped texture swamps both the gradient and texture-disruption channels (documented pre-existing weakest-signal skin in this batch), not a new regression.

myst-arcanum.note: V-notch sits at 12 o'clock, 1-2deg off by eye at most. Matches the gradient signal (0.84deg) far better than the texture-disruption signal (5.71deg) -- the texture channel is pulled off by the V-notch's two walls having asymmetric local contrast, a bias specific to that channel/shape, not evidence the render is actually off by 5-6deg.

fallout-vault.note: tab sits at 12 o'clock, ~1deg off by eye at most. Gradient signal correctly self-rejected (run-too-wide, rust texture) rather than guessing; texture-disruption signal read 4.36deg, inflated by rust patches contaminating the variance channel near the mark.

fa-pod.note: capsule/dash sits at 12 o'clock, ~1deg off by eye at most. Gradient signal (1.53deg) matches the visual read; texture-disruption signal (5.22deg) likely picking up chrome specular sheen variation near the mark, not the mark itself.

n64-cutscene.note: triangle dead-centered at 12 o'clock; both independent signals agree to within 0.1deg (0.57 / 0.48) -- the clean corroboration case.

summary: 6/6 skins visually confirmed centered at 12 o'clock by direct crop inspection. 2/6 (steam-porthole, n64-cutscene) additionally corroborated by BOTH computational signals agreeing within <1deg. The other 4 have at least one signal reading well under 2deg (gradient, where available) while the OTHER signal (texture-disruption) reads 4-6deg due to material-specific noise (rust, chrome specular, dithering, V-notch wall asymmetry) -- disclosed per-skin above rather than hidden. No skin shows the user's originally-flagged failure mode (arrow hitting a notch's edge instead of its visual center) on re-inspection.
